prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
Sorry to hear you were in an accident — that’s stressful. I can’t tell you a single “best” lawyer to hire, but I can help you choose the right personal-injury attorney in Pleasanton by giving practical criteria, questions to ask, next steps, and resources. If you want, I can also pull together a short list of local attorneys for you to contact.

Immediate steps to take (if you haven’t already)
- Seek medical attention now and follow doctors’ orders. Medical records are crucial evidence.
- Report the accident to police and to your insurance company (give facts only).
- Preserve evidence: photos of vehicles, injuries, road conditions; witness names/phones; medical bills; receipts; repair estimates.
- Don’t post details or photos about the accident on social media.
- Avoid giving recorded statements to the at-fault party’s insurer without counsel.

Important deadlines
- California personal injury statute of limitations is generally 2 years from the injury date. (Wrongful death is also generally 2 years.)
- If a government vehicle/agency is involved, you usually have only 6 months to file a government claim. Get an attorney quickly in that case.

How to choose the right lawyer — key criteria
- Experience with car-accident cases and settlements/trials in California courts.
- Local knowledge of Alameda County courts, judges, and defense firms.
- Trial experience (many cases settle, but you want someone willing to go to trial if needed).
- Track record of recoveries and client testimonials (not just advertising claims).
- Who will actually handle your case — the named partner or a junior associate?
- Clear fee structure and transparency about costs and contingency fee percentage.
- Good communication: timely responses and clear explanations.
- No disciplinary history (check the State Bar of California).

Questions to ask at an initial consultation
- Do you handle car-accident injury cases? How long have you done this?
- What percentage of your practice is car-accident/personal injury?
- What is your contingency fee and who pays out-of-pocket costs (litigation costs, medical liens) if we don’t recover?
- Who will work on my case day-to-day? Will you personally handle negotiations and court appearances?
- What is your track record of verdicts/settlements for similar cases?
- Do you have references from past clients?
- What do you think a fair settlement range is for my case and why?
- How long do you think my case will take?
- How often will you update me and by what method (phone/email)?

Red flags to watch for
- Pressure to sign immediately or guarantees of a specific dollar amount.
- Vague answers about who will handle the case or how fees/costs are handled.
- Poor online reviews about communication or missed deadlines.
- Any disciplinary sanctions on the State Bar record.

Typical fees and costs
- Most personal-injury lawyers in California work on contingency (commonly 33–40% of the recovery if the case settles before trial; percentages can change for trial or appeal).
- Expect the firm to advance litigation costs (medical records, expert witnesses) and be reimbursed from the recovery.
- Ask for a written fee agreement before signing.

Where to find and check attorneys
- State Bar of California lawyer search (to verify license and disciplinary history).
- Alameda County Bar Association or local referral services.
- Lawyer directories (Martindale-Hubbell, local Google/Yelp/Avvo) — use reviews as one data point, not the sole decision-maker.
- Ask friends, family, or medical providers for recommendations.

If you want, I can:
- Find and list 3–5 Pleasanton/Alameda County personal-injury attorneys with contact info and quick notes on experience.
- Draft an email/phone script you can use to screen attorneys.
- Help you prepare documents to bring to consultations.

If you’d like a shortlist, tell me:
- Any injuries and whether you’ve already seen a doctor,
- Whether the other driver was cited/insured and the insurers involved,
- Any deadline concerns (e.g., government vehicle involved),
- Any preferences (trial lawyer, bilingual, budget concerns).
